title: Dental emergency? Start here
lead: Most dental problems can wait for the next open slot — but some can't. Here's what to do right now.
hospitalWarning: Go to a hospital emergency department immediately for swelling that spreads to the eye or neck, difficulty breathing or swallowing, high fever with facial swelling, a jaw injury, or bleeding that won't stop after 20 minutes of firm pressure.

situations.title: Severe toothache
steps: Rinse with warm salt water and gently floss to remove trapped food.
Take a painkiller you normally use safely, following the pack instructions. Don't put tablets on the gum.
Call the clinic to be seen as soon as possible.

situations.title: Knocked-out adult tooth
steps: Pick it up by the crown (the white part), not the root.
If it is dirty, rinse briefly in milk — do not scrub it.
Push it back into the socket if you can and bite on a clean cloth; otherwise keep it in milk.
Come to the clinic within the hour if at all possible.

situations.title: Broken or chipped tooth
steps: Rinse your mouth with warm water and keep any pieces.
Use a cold pack on the cheek for swelling.
Call the clinic for the next available appointment.

situations.title: Swelling of the face or gum
steps: Hold a cold compress against the cheek — never a hot one.
Call the clinic the same day.
If the swelling spreads quickly, or you have fever or trouble swallowing, go to a hospital emergency department.

situations.title: Bleeding after an extraction
steps: Bite firmly on a folded clean gauze or cloth for 20–30 minutes without checking.
Sit upright and avoid rinsing or spitting.
If bleeding is still heavy after that, call the clinic or go to a hospital.
